transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Um, I came in because I’ve barely been sleeping since a warehouse inspection I had to do for work. I just lie in bed replaying bits of it in my head. And when I do actually manage to drift off, I wake up completely sweaty and wide awake... it just feels like I’m right back near that blast.
Do upsetting memories of the blast pop into your mind during the day even when you’re not trying to think about it?

Yeah, they do. Um, I’ll just be at work, reviewing a policy or looking at a loss report, and suddenly I get hit with this really sharp image of the worker on the floor and all the soot in the air. It just... it feels like my body reacts to it before I can even stop it.
Since the blast, have you been avoiding reminders of it?

Yeah, I have. Um... I've actually been avoiding that specific warehouse file at work. And I've been letting any calls about our industrial accounts just go straight to voicemail. Honestly, even just the thought of opening those emails makes my stomach drop... so I just stay away from it as much as I can.
How long ago did the warehouse blast happen?
It happened about a week ago. That's when I had to do the inspection and... yeah, all this has been going on since then.
Since the blast, have there been moments when you felt like you were actually back at the scene, as if it were happening again?

No, I don't think so. I mean, the memories are really strong, like I said, but I always know I'm at work or at home. I don't actually lose touch with where I am or feel like I'm physically back in the warehouse.
Since the blast, have you found that you can’t remember an important part of what happened during the inspection?

Yeah, actually. Um... I can remember hearing the explosion, and I can clearly remember standing outside afterward with soot on my jacket. But the part in between is just completely blank. No matter how hard I try to piece it together, I just can't remember how I got from inside the warehouse to the outside.
Have these symptoms lasted longer than a month since the blast?

No, not a month. Like I mentioned a little bit ago, it's really only been about a week. All of this just started right after that warehouse inspection where the explosion happened, so it hasn't been anywhere near a month yet.
Since the blast, have you felt detached from yourself, like you were watching yourself from the outside or that things around you didn’t feel real?

No, I haven't really felt anything like that. I don't feel disconnected from my body or like I'm watching myself, and everything around me still feels real... just, you know, stressful. But no, I haven't had any of those out-of-body feelings.
Since the blast, have you been getting jumpy or startling more easily than usual?

Yes, definitely. Um... especially at work. Every time a printer jams, or a door slams, or even if someone just comes up behind my desk, I jump. It's like I instantly think something terrible is happening. And then it takes me several minutes to just... settle down and get my breath back.
Since the blast, have you been unable to feel positive emotions, like feeling happy, close to other people, or hopeful?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I can still feel happy about things. I still feel close to my friends and family. It's not like all the good feelings are gone, it's just... I'm just really on edge and stressed out all the time. But I can still smile and feel hopeful about the future.
When these memories hit, do you ever feel for a moment like the explosion is happening again right now?

No, I don't think I've had that happen. When I think about it, I know it's just a memory. I don't feel like I'm actually back there or that it's happening all over again. It's just a really clear, upsetting memory, but I always know where I am right now.
During the explosion or immediately afterward, did you feel emotionally numb or dazed?

No, I don't think I felt numb at all. I mean, I was terrified, obviously, and just completely panicked right when it happened. But... no, I wasn't dazed. I knew exactly what was going on and I just wanted to get out of there as fast as I could.
